cases.title: 아름다운 as an adjective
cases.why: The adjective 'beautiful' shares its stem with the name 아름. A stem-prefix match would be a false positive.

ambiguity.note: The adjective ending 다운 and the noun 풍경 make it a modifier.

cases.title: Given name 아름 with informal suffix 이
cases.why: 아름 means 'beauty' (as in 아름답다) and is a given name; the informal suffix and an action predicate select a person.

ambiguity.note: Opening a door is a human action.

cases.title: 바다가 좋다: like the sea or like Bada
cases.why: 좋다 ('is good/likes') fits both a noun (the sea is nice) and a person (Bada is nice); nothing in the text resolves it.

ambiguity.note: Both a sea and a person named Bada can be 'good', and the sentence is context-free.

cases.title: Given name 바다 as a person arriving
cases.why: 바다 means 'sea' and is also used as a given name. An arrival predicate selects a person.

ambiguity.note: 'Arrived first' requires an animate subject.

cases.title: Noun 바다 in a view description
cases.why: Partner of bada-name-and-sea: the same syllables with a view predicate denote the sea.

ambiguity.note: 'Was visible through the window' describes a landscape feature.

cases.title: 봄이 왔다: spring came or Bom came
cases.why: 봄이 왔다 is the standard idiom for 'spring has come' but is grammatical for a person named 봄 arriving.

ambiguity.note: The idiom reads as the season arriving; a person named Bom arriving is equally well-formed in isolation.

cases.title: Name 이봄 beside the season 봄 (spring)
cases.why: 봄 means 'spring' and is a given name; a two-syllable name (surname plus 봄).

ambiguity.note: A person is born in a season; the first token takes the topic marker as the subject.

cases.title: Full name 이보람 who has finished a presentation
cases.why: 보람 means 'worth/reward' and is a given name; a presentation predicate selects a person.

ambiguity.note: Finishing a presentation is a human action.

cases.title: Noun 보람 in 'it was worth it'
cases.why: Partner of boram-name: the abstract noun in an idiomatic phrase, with no human referent.

ambiguity.note: 'There was worth in having worked' uses the noun in a fixed expression.

cases.title: Name 김별 beside the noun 별 (star)
cases.why: 별 means 'star' and is also a given name; the full name is a person and the bare noun is a celestial body.

ambiguity.note: 'Likes the stars in the night sky' marks the noun; the first token is a full name.

cases.title: 별이 예쁘다: the star is pretty or Byeol is pretty
cases.why: 예쁘다 ('is pretty') fits a star (별) or a person named 별.

ambiguity.note: A star can be pretty and so can a person called Byeol; no disambiguating context exists.

cases.title: 가을이 보고 싶다: miss Gaeul or want to see autumn
cases.why: As with 하늘이 보고 싶다, the verb fits both a season and a person named 가을.

ambiguity.note: Both 'I want to see autumn' and 'I miss Gaeul' are natural readings.

cases.title: Name 김가을 beside the season 가을 (autumn)
cases.why: 가을 means 'autumn' and is a given name; one sentence has the full name and the season.

ambiguity.note: The first token is a full name with a topic marker; the second is the season as the object of 'likes most'.

cases.title: 가람 as an archaic word for 'river'
cases.why: 가람 is a poetic word for 'river' and a given name; a flowing predicate selects the noun.

ambiguity.note: Flowing slowly is predicated of a river.

cases.title: 가람 as a given name
cases.why: Partner of garam-old-word-river: a presentation predicate selects a person.

ambiguity.note: Finishing a presentation is a human action.

cases.title: 김치우는: 김치 우는 vs 김치우 는 in a context-free fragment
cases.why: In spacing-free text, 김치우는 can be the name 김치우 plus the topic marker 는 or the words 김치 and 우는; as a bare fragment it is undecidable.

ambiguity.note: '김치우는 모습이' parses as a person's appearance or as 'kimchi's crying look'; the second reading is odd but the text does not exclude it.

cases.title: Given name 하늘 with informal suffix 이
cases.why: The bare given name 하늘 appears with the euphonic suffix 이 and topic marker 는; the noun 'sky' would not take a person-referring predicate like 전학을 왔다.

ambiguity.note: 'Transferred to a new school' needs an animate subject, so the otherwise-common noun is a person.

cases.title: 하늘이 보고 싶다: miss Haneul or want to see the sky
cases.why: 보고 싶다 means both 'want to see' and 'miss'. With 하늘 (sky, and a given name) as subject marker holder, the sentence is undecidable from text alone.

ambiguity.note: Both 'I want to see the sky' and 'I miss Haneul' are natural; no other context is given.

cases.title: Name 김하늘 beside the noun 하늘 (sky)
cases.why: The given name 하늘 is also the word for sky. One sentence contains both: the full name is a person, the bare noun is not.

ambiguity.note: The first token includes a surname and takes a topic marker; the second is the object of 'saw' and is the sky.

cases.title: 한결 as the adverb 'much more'
cases.why: Partner of hangyeol-given-name: the adverb modifies a verb.

ambiguity.note: 'The weather got better' is modified by the adverb 한결; no person is referred to.

cases.title: Given name 한결 with informal suffix
cases.why: 한결 means 'consistently/much more' as an adverb and is a given name; the euphonic suffix and an arrival predicate select a person.

ambiguity.note: Being the first to arrive requires an animate subject.

cases.title: 한울 as a given name
cases.why: Partner of hanul-wide-sky: an arrival predicate selects a person.

ambiguity.note: Arriving is a human action here.

cases.title: 한울 as 'the great sky'
cases.why: 한울 is an archaic word for 'the great sky' and a given name; a predicate of extent selects the noun.

ambiguity.note: Being endlessly wide describes the sky.

cases.title: Given name 하루 alone
cases.why: 하루 means 'one day' and is a given name; an arrival predicate selects a person.

ambiguity.note: Arriving first requires an animate subject.

cases.title: 하루 as 'one day'
cases.why: Partner of haru-given-name: the same syllables as a time noun.

ambiguity.note: A day that was too long; the noun is the subject of an evaluation.

cases.title: Name 김이슬 beside the noun 이슬 (dew)
cases.why: 이슬 means 'dew' and is also a given name; one sentence contains the full name and the noun.

ambiguity.note: 'Saw the dew on the grass blade' is a nature description; the first token is a full name.

cases.title: 정원이 예쁘다: the garden is pretty or Jeongwon is pretty
cases.why: 정원 means garden and is a common given name; an evaluative predicate does not resolve it.

ambiguity.note: A garden can be pretty and so can a person named Jeongwon.

cases.title: 지혜 with a dative marker
cases.why: Partner of jihye-borrow-wisdom: the dative 에게 marks the source of a borrowed book, which must be a person.

ambiguity.note: 에게 marks an animate recipient or source.

cases.title: 지혜를 빌리다 as a fixed phrase
cases.why: 지혜 means 'wisdom' and is a very common given name. 지혜를 빌리다 is an idiom meaning to seek advice.

ambiguity.note: The collocation 지혜를 빌리다 means to rely on someone's wisdom, with no individual named.

cases.title: 진주 as an early arriver
cases.why: Partner of jinju-locative: the subject marker 가 with an arrival predicate selects a person.

ambiguity.note: Arriving first is predicated of an animate subject marked with 가.

cases.title: 진주 with a locative particle
cases.why: 진주 is a city, a gem and a given name. The locative 에서 after it selects a place.

ambiguity.note: 에서 marks the place of an event; as a person it would need a different postposition.

cases.title: 마루 as a wooden floor
cases.why: 마루 means 'wooden floor' and is a given name; the locative 에 and a sitting predicate select the noun.

ambiguity.note: Sitting and resting 'on' a surface selects the floor.

cases.title: Given name 마루 with a particle
cases.why: Partner of marul-floor-noun: a person who is late.

ambiguity.note: Being late is a human behavior.

cases.title: 미소 with a possessor
cases.why: Partner of miso-smile-either: a possessive 그녀의 before the word makes it a possessed noun.

ambiguity.note: A possessor phrase selects a body-part or expression noun.

cases.title: 미소가 아름다웠다: a smile or Miso
cases.why: 미소 means 'smile' and is a given name; a bare subject with 아름다웠다 ('was beautiful') fits both.

ambiguity.note: A smile can be beautiful and so can a person; nothing marks a possessor or an honorific.

cases.title: 미소 as a vocative
cases.why: Partner of miso-smile-either: the vocative 야 addresses a person.

ambiguity.note: The vocative particle 야 and the imperative 이리 와 ('come here') address a person.

cases.title: Name 최사랑 beside the noun 사랑 (love)
cases.why: 사랑 means 'love' and is used as a given name; both appear in one sentence.

ambiguity.note: 'The love that X spoke of' contains the abstract noun; the first token is a full name.

cases.title: 슬기롭게 derived from the noun 슬기
cases.why: A derived adverb ('wisely') built on the same syllables; the whole word is not a person mention and a prefix match on 슬기 would be a false positive.

ambiguity.note: The adverb suffix 롭게 turns the noun into 'wisely'.

cases.title: Given name 슬기 with topic marker 는
cases.why: 슬기 means 'wisdom' and is a very common given name for women; an early-arrival predicate selects a person.

ambiguity.note: Arriving early is a human action.

cases.title: 송이 as a counter for grapes
cases.why: Partner of songi-name: the same syllables as a counter noun for clusters (a bunch of grapes).

ambiguity.note: The counter follows the noun 포도 'grape' and the numeral 한.

cases.title: Given name 송이 as a person
cases.why: 송이 is a given name; as 'cluster' it is a counter and as 송이버섯 a mushroom. An arrival predicate selects a person.

ambiguity.note: Arriving early is a human action.

cases.title: Given name 소리 beside the noun 소리 (sound)
cases.why: 소리 means 'sound' and is used as a given name; one sentence holds both.

ambiguity.note: The first token is a full name; the second is the object of 'heard'.

cases.title: 소원 with an informal-name suffix
cases.why: Partner of sowon-wish-granted: the informal-name suffix 이 plus 는 and a school predicate select a child.

ambiguity.note: 이는 attaches to a person's given name and going to school is a human action.

cases.title: 소원 as a wish
cases.why: 소원 means 'wish' and is an uncommon given name; 이루어졌다 ('came true') is predicated of wishes.

ambiguity.note: Coming true is predicated of wishes.

cases.title: Name 박여름 beside the season 여름 (summer)
cases.why: 여름 means 'summer' and is a given name; both occur in one sentence with opposite roles.

ambiguity.note: The full name is the subject; the season is a time adverbial with the locative 에.

cases.title: 이 대리가 왔다: this deputy or Deputy Lee
cases.why: 이 is both the demonstrative 'this' and the surname 이; 이 대리 is therefore 'this assistant manager' or 'Assistant Manager Lee'.

ambiguity.note: Without prior mention of a deputy, 이 may be the demonstrative or the surname.

cases.title: 이 과장님은 휴가다: this manager or Manager Lee
cases.why: Another 이 + title pattern where demonstrative and surname readings are both grammatical.

ambiguity.note: A section chief is on vacation: the demonstrative 'this' and the surname Lee both parse.

cases.title: 윤슬이 반짝였다: the water glitter sparkled or Yunseul sparkled
cases.why: 윤슬 means sunlight glittering on water and is a recent given name; 반짝이다 ('sparkle') fits the noun literally and a person figuratively.

ambiguity.note: The literal reading is the water glitter; a person sparkling figuratively is possible, and no context decides.
